BEFORE THE GEORGIA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION

Georgia Power CompanyGeorgia Power Company
Docket Nos. 44280, 56002, 56003
2022 Base Rate Case
2025 IRP & DSM Filings
STF-NU1 Data Request Set No. 1 

BASIS FOR THE ASSERTION THAT THE 
INFORMATION SUBMITTED IS A TRADE SECRET


	Georgia Power Company (“Georgia Power” or the “Company”) submits to the Georgia Public Service Commission as part of its Nuclear Uprate Application and Tariff Filing in Docket Nos. 44280, 56002, and 56003 its response to STF-NU1-1-3 (“Response”). In the Response, the Company has provided confidential nuclear uprate project costs and projected program subscription costs (the “Information”). All such Information constitutes trade secret Information of the Southern Company, Georgia Power, and its affiliates and is therefore protected from public disclosure under Commission Rule 515-3-1-.11.

	The Information derives economic value from not being generally known to and not being readily ascertainable by proper means by other persons who can obtain economic value from its disclosure or use. Specifically, the Information contains confidential unit-specific uprate project costs along with projected program costs. Publicly disclosing the Information would allow bidders and vendors to tailor proposals according to the Company’s expected costs, setting an artificial floor on bidding to the detriment and harm of the Company and its customers. Disclosure of the trade secret portions of the Information could also prevent the Company from adequately soliciting and obtaining the best cost estimates for future consulting work and harm the Company’s efforts to obtain optimal pricing in current or future negotiations, harming customers as well as Georgia Power. Finally, the Company’s competitors are not required to disclose similar information and to require Georgia Power to do so would put it at an economic disadvantage. 

	The Information is subject to substantial procedures to maintain its secrecy. Only select Georgia Power and Southern Company Services personnel are granted access to the Information. Those personnel receive access only on a “need to know” basis. Parties outside the Company who have been granted access to the Information, if any, have been required to sign confidentiality agreements with respect to the Information.

	The Information is subject to substantial procedures to maintain its secrecy. Only select Georgia Power and Southern Company Services personnel are granted access to the Information. Those personnel receive access only on a “need to know” basis. Parties outside the Company who have been granted access to the Information, if any, have been required to sign confidentiality agreements with respect to the Information.

STF-NU1-1-4

Question: 

“Each participating customer will pay a Program Enrollment Contribution (PEC) and an NU-1 tariff Monthly Subscription Payment that will be separate and in addition to the cost of electric service under the customer’s then-existing retail electric service tariff. In exchange for the Monthly Subscription Payment, each participating customer will receive zero emission credits (ZECs) in an amount based on the customer’s subscription level and the corresponding pro-rata share of the output of the Nuclear Uprate Portfolio, measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh).” How will the PEC and Monthly Subscription Payment amounts be calculated? Please provide the Company’s estimates for the PEC and monthly subscription payment.

Response:

Please see STF-NU1-1-4 Attachment TRADE SECRET for supporting information related to the calculation of the PEC and ZEC amounts. The model also contains annual estimates for the PEC and ZEC payment amounts. Based on the Company's current program design and economic analysis, the estimated PEC is $███████████, structured as three annual installment payments of $██████████ per year scheduled prior to the in-service dates of the uprated units. The ongoing ZEC price is $███/MWh during the term of the customer agreement, and the Monthly Subscription Payment will be calculated by multiplying the ZEC price by the Uprate Capacity Energy Share.

The economic data presented in STF-NU1-1-4 Attachment TRADE SECRET.xlsx has been updated since the time of this request. Please see the B26_AV_Tool_HatchEPU - GPC Ownership TRADE SECRET.xlsx workpapers submitted in the Application for Approval of the 2026 Plant Hatch Units 1-2 Nuclear Extended Power Uprates filing.

=== DKT 56002 STF-NU1-1 PUBLIC DISCLOSURE/STF-NU1-1-9.docx ===
STF-NU1-1-9

Question: 

Please explain how the NU-1 tariff will benefit non- subscribing customers of Georgia Power.

Response:

Non-subscribing customers benefit from the NU-1 tariff through subscriber payments collected through the tariff in exchange for the carbon free attributes generated by the uprate projects. These subscriber payments significantly offset the revenue requirements of the uprate projects during construction and throughout the term of the customer agreement. In addition to the reduced revenue requirements for the projects, non-subscribing customers also benefit from the additional capacity value and energy savings resulting from the uprate projects.  

=== DKT 56002 STF-NU1-1 PUBLIC DISCLOSURE/STF-NU1-1-13 - Trade Secret Assertion.docx ===
BEFORE THE GEORGIA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION

Georgia Power Company
Docket No. 44280, 56002, 56003 
2022 Base Rate Case 
2025 IRP & DSM Filings 
STF-NU1 Data Request Set No. 1 

BASIS FOR THE ASSERTION THAT THE
INFORMATION SUBMITTED IS A TRADE SECRET
 
Georgia Power Company (“Georgia Power” or the “Company”) submits to the Georgia Public Service Commission as part of its Nuclear Uprate Application and Tariff Filing in Docket Nos. 44280, 56002, and 56003 its response to STF-NU1-1-13 (“Response”). In the Responses, the Company has provided a presentation given to the Georgia Public Service Commission Public Interest Advocacy Staff on the Nuclear Uprate Subscription Program, including confidential data, information, and proprietary assumptions used in the development of the Company’s Nuclear Uprate Subscription Program (the “Information”). All such Information constitutes trade secret Information of the Southern Company, Georgia Power, and its affiliates and is therefore protected from public disclosure under Commission Rule 515-3-1-.11

	The Information derives economic value from not being generally known to, and not being readily ascertainable by proper means by, other persons who can obtain economic value from its disclosure or use. Specifically, the Information contains competitively sensitive data and assumptions relative to the Company’s development and pricing of its Nuclear Uprate Subscription Program. Public dissemination of the Information would allow Georgia Power’s competitors and potential program participants access to the Company’s subscription program pricing strategies and objectives, thereby bestowing insight into the Company’s strategic initiatives and pricing strategies. The Information, if disseminated, could provide insight to competitors regarding the Company’s Nuclear Uprate Subscription Program and may influence participation in or alter their Competitors offers to large load customers, to the detriment of Georgia Power and its customers. If the Company were to publicly disseminate the Information, Georgia Power customers would potentially lose out on economic benefits brought on by participation in the Nuclear Uprate Subscription Program. Competitors would obtain an unfair advantage because they are not required to reveal similar information and can structure similar programs based on the Information rather than their own costs, capacity, abilities, strategies, or analysis.

	The Information is subject to substantial procedures to maintain its secrecy. Only select Georgia Power and Southern Company Services personnel are granted access to the Information. Those personnel receive access only on a “need to know” basis. Parties outside the Company who have been granted access to the Information, if any, have been required to sign confidentiality agreements with respect to the Information. 

=== DKT 56002 STF-NU1-1 PUBLIC DISCLOSURE/STF-NU1-1-10.docx ===
STF-NU1-1-10

Question: 

What happens to the incremental revenue from the NU-1 tariff? Identify and explain the accounting treatment for all revenue and expenses associated with the tariff. Does this accounting treatment differ from what is required by accounting standards? Regarding the proposed accounting treatment, what specifically does Georgia Power have to receive approval from the Commission?

Response:

The Company is proposing to collect revenues under the NU-1 tariff associated with the nuclear uprate project in two ways.

The Program Enrollment Contribution (“PEC”) will be collected from subscribers prior to the in-service date of the Plant Hatch uprate project and will be recognized as a prepaid liability under the accounting guidelines. The prepaid revenue will be amortized over the assumed remaining life of the asset to other operating revenues, which will reduce retail cost of service for retail customers. The Company does not require separate approval from the Commission for this accounting treatment. However, as discussed with Staff and per the Company's Application for Approval of the 2026 Plant Hatch Units 1-2 Nuclear Extended Power Uprates, the Company is requesting Commission approval for the following accounting treatment. For any PEC payments received from the tariff subscribers in 2028, the Company will apply the payments to CWIP base in 2028 solely for the purposes of calculating AFUDC on the project and the payment will be excluded from retail rate base. Beginning in 2029, any PEC payments will be applied as a reduction to retail rate base following GAAP accounting and will be reflected as such in the 2028 base rate case projections. In the event the current Alternate Rate Plan (“ARP”) is extended beyond 2028, any further application of the PEC payments to CWIP base shall be considered as part of the ARP extension. 

The Zero Emission Credit (“ZEC”) revenue will be collected from subscribers once the nuclear uprate is in-service and recognized as collected under the accounting guidelines. This revenue will be recorded to other operating revenues and reduce retail cost of service for retail customers. The Company does not require separate approval from the Commission for this accounting treatment. However, as discussed with Staff and per the Company's Application for Approval of the 2026 Plant Hatch Units 1-2 Nuclear Extended Power Uprates, the Company is requesting Commission approval for the following accounting treatment. Any ZEC payments received from the tariff subscribers through December 31, 2028, will be recorded as a regulatory liability until the next base rate case. If the ARP is further extended, deferral of ZEC payments beyond 2028 will be considered as part of the terms of the extension. Beginning January 1, 2029, any ZEC payments received from the tariff subscribers will be trued-up on an actual basis to the projected amounts included in the next base rate case.

In order to mitigate revenue requirement impacts to non-subscribing customers before the full benefits of uprated capacity can be realized, the Company is requesting approval from the Commission to defer depreciation and interest expenses associated with the Plant Hatch project capital cost closed to plant in service. The deferred depreciation and interest expenses are proposed to be amortized over the life of the asset once the project is complete and uprate projects reach commercial operation date (“COD”). Amortization of the deferred depreciation and interest would begin in the month the incremental uprate capacity is placed in service and begins generating incremental electricity through the end of the life of the units, aligning cost recovery with the start of incremental generation and the associated project benefits.

=== DKT 56002 STF-NU1-1 PUBLIC DISCLOSURE/STF-NU1-1-7.docx ===
STF-NU1-1-7

Question: 

“To subscribe to the NU-1 tariff, a customer must execute a customer agreement with Georgia Power. The customer’s subscription term under the NU-1 tariff will coincide with the term of the Nuclear Uprate Customer Agreement as selected by the customer during the NOI process. Such term may be up to 25 years.” Is there a minimum subscription term under the tariff (e.g. 10 years, 15 years)?

Response:

The Company anticipates that customer agreements will be for a 25-year term, consistent with the program's capital recovery structure and the subscriber’s long-term clean energy commitments. There is no minimum term threshold required under the NU-1 Tariff.

=== DKT 56002 STF-NU1-1 PUBLIC DISCLOSURE/STF-NU1-1-2.docx ===
STF-NU1-1-2

Question: 

“An eligible customer wishing to subscribe to the NU-1 tariff must submit a Notice of Intent (NOI) to sponsor the nuclear uprate program and pay a one-time sponsorship fee.” How long will the NOI period be open? How much is the sponsorship fee? Please describe how the amount was determined and provide workpapers supporting any calculations used to determine the amount.

Response:

Georgia Power has modified the proposed enrollment process to a first come, first served process, instead of an open NOI period. The Company has communicated with a subset of customers (please refer to the response to STF-NU1-1-23) to gauge interest in this program, and expects a single customer to enroll and subscribe to all the ZECs made available through this tariff at this time. As part of the development of the NU-1 tariff, the Company has executed a term sheet and commenced contract discussions with a single qualifying customer. The enrollment process will be further evaluated and potentially modified upon the availability of future uprate subscriptions, if any. 

=== DKT 56002 STF-NU1-1 PUBLIC DISCLOSURE/STF-NU1-1-1.docx ===
STF-NU1-1-1

Question: 

Refer to the Company’s draft Nuclear Uprates “NU-1” Electric Service Tariff. The new tariff availability states: “Available throughout Georgia Power Company’s service area.” Does the service territory include all large load customers being served by Georgia Power Company, including those being served as a result of the customer choice program?

Response:

Yes. The NU-1 tariff is available to all Georgia Power customers that meet the applicability criteria, including large load customers considered “customer choice” as defined in Georgia’s Territorial Act.

=== DKT 56002 STF-NU1-1 PUBLIC DISCLOSURE/STF-NU1-1-8.docx ===
STF-NU1-1-8

Question: 

“If Georgia Power terminates a customer agreement due to an event of default by customer, the customer will be responsible for damages and payments in accordance with the customer’s agreement.” How is default defined in the customer agreement? How will damages be calculated?

Response:

Termination of the agreement due to customer default will result in the customer paying any remaining Program Enrollment Credit (“PEC”) payments, if applicable, plus the amount of lost Zero-Emission Credit (“ZEC”) revenue, which will be equal to the aggregate sum of the amount of ZECs expected to be produced by each uprate unit during the remaining term of the agreement times the ZEC price.

In the event that Commission Staff do not recommend certification of the Hatch Unit upgrades before customers sign customer agreements fully committing to pay for the uprates, explain why customer agreements cannot include a contingency, or “regulatory out,” providing that the agreement would be terminated in the event that the Commission does not approve the upgrades.

Question: 

Based on the costs discussed during the 3/19 meeting with Staff, how many customers do the Company anticipate will enroll in this tariff?

Response:
